title: MODULAR MODE: Select a Block in the Modular Configurator Window
content: ### Objective Select and combine Blocks as desired in the Modular Configurator window. ### Location Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ Modular Configurator ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ Modular Configurator → Modular Configurator window appears. 2\. Select a desired category from the horizontal tab. → Folders appear in order. 3\. Select a desired Garment category folder. → Modular Structure file is displayed. 4\. content: ### Objective Open files that are auto-saved when the program closes unexpectedly due to a power failure or error. ※ Note: * From ver3.1.0, project file (*.zprj) will be auto saved. * File is auto saved every three minutes. Therefore, auto save files only contains work completed three minutes prior to power/ program failure. ### Location #### By Opening the Program Launch Marvelous Designer ▶ Auto Save File pop-up #### By Locating the File C: ▶ Users ▶ User Name ▶ Documents ▶ Marvelous Designer ▶ Assets_ver_x.x.x ▶ Autosave ### Operation #### By Opening the Program 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Launch Marvelous Designer ▶ Auto Save File pop-up → The auto-saved file opens. #### By Opening the Folder 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: C: ▶ Users ▶ User Name ▶ Documents ▶ Marvelous Designer ▶ Assets_ver_x.x.x ▶ Autosave 2. Double-click autosave.zpac/ autosave.zprj file created in the folder. → The program starts and the auto saved file opens. ※ Note: #### Auto Save File Location You can changed the folder in which Auto Save files are saved via (ver2.3.0): Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Default Files ▶ Auto Save ▶ Select file path
content_description: This page provides instructions for accessing auto-saved files in Marvelous Designer following unexpected program closures or power failures.

title: MODULAR MODE: Module Structure
content: Module is a system that allows you to adjust the designs easily and combine them part by part. Please see the terminology for the Module below in order to have a better understanding in the Modular Mode. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438537801881) A: Module Structure: A state when a Block Box that consists of a Garment is sewn to another. When sewing a Block Box that is in this Block Structure to a Pattern, it automatically creates Sewing Lines in between the Patterns as it is already interlocked. B: Pattern: Patterns to be included in a Block that will be adjusted partially. Patterns in the Modular Mode can be modified and sewn the same as the Simulation Mode. C: Block Box: A frame that consists of a Module Structure. D: Block: A state when Patterns are sewn to Block Boxes. Blocks that have the same Block Boxes can be replaced with each other.
content_description: Discover the Modular Mode, where you can effortlessly customize and combine designs by adjusting garments, patterns, and block structures for a seamless sewing experience.

title: UV EDITOR MODE: Change Normal Map Blending Method
content: ### Objective This feature allows users to select the Normal Map Blending Method that provides the best results for their intended use. ### Location Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ Graphic Options ▶ Normal Map Blending ### Operation 1. Load garment with a blended normal map component, → Example: Topstitching with the Type changed to "Texture" and the check box next to "3D" activated in the Property Editor. 2. Change a window view mode to UV Editor, and change the display channel to Normal Map. 3. Open Settings/Preferences in the Main Menu at the top of the interface, then select 'Preferences'. → Move the Preferences window so that it does not cover the UV Editor. 4. In the Preferences window, under Graphics Options, change the 'Normal Blending Method'. → Observe the normal map for blended Normal Map components is changed. 5. Bake out the normal map using the 'Bake Textures' option at the top of the UV Editor for application to the garment in an external 3D environment.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on selecting and adjusting the Normal Map Blending Method to optimize visual results for garment design in 3D environments.

title: Requesting Network Software License activation - First Time installation (Mac OS)
content: **[Software License Key for Network Offline] Generate a C2V for First Time Installation - Mac OS** **1\. Install a Run-time Environment on Mac OS following by steps below (step1, step2)** **Step 1.** Unzip Sentinel_Runtime.tar ([Sentinel Runtime](https://s3.amazonaws.com/s3.md.web.upload/newmdweb/helpcenter/installer/Sentinel_Runtime.tar) **Download**) **Step 2.** Run SentinelRuntimeInstallerCLI (Command Line Interface) and install on Mac’s terminal Once you are completed with steps above(step1, step2), you’re ready to generate a C2V file for the first time installation of an SL key. **Step 3.** Open a web browser and navigate to **[ACC Page](http://localhost:1947)** **Step 4.** Click on the “Fingerprint” button to create a C2V file. ![pasted_image_0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438507392153) **Step 5.** Submit your C2V file to this [**page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (Login with company account is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com **Step 6.** Please refer below to complete a V2C key update. **[Applying a V2C on the server]** 1\. Download the V2C file sent from Marvelous Designer Support Team. 2\. Click on the link below to access the ACC Page, then select “Update/Attach” in Options on the left. **(Click here to link[ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html))** ![v2c_application_1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438479628185) 3\. Click “Choose File” to find and select the downloaded V2C file. ![v2c_application_2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438479878297) 4\. Click “Apply File”. 5\. If the update is successful, the following message will be printed. ![v2c_application_3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438507936921) **[Double checking an updated License Key]** If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and navigate to [**ACC Page**](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 2\. Click Features once you see the key info. ![v2c_application_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438480194073) 3\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed to the correct number. ![v2c_application_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438508320025)
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for generating a C2V file and updating a software license key for first-time installation on Mac OS, ensuring a smooth offline setup process.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Buckling Stiffness
content: ### Objective Adjust how much percentage (%) of total Bending intensity to use to decide the Buckling Stiffness of the corners of Fabric. This is used alongside Bending-Weft/Warp. For instance, entering a Buckling Stiffness of 80 when Bending value is 60, is going to result in the Bending value of the actual intensity of the part of the Fabric being folded being 80% of 60 which is 48. In other words, the higher the Buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the corners of fabric, and on the other hand, the lower the the ratio, the easier it folds. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ Buckling Stiffness-Weft/Warp ![____.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438785993753)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the percentage of total bending intensity to determine the buckling stiffness of fabric corners, facilitating optimal folding performance in fabric design.

title: [Mode] SCULPT
content: ### Objective Sculpt garments using various brush tools. (ver. 8) ### Location SCULPT Mode Brush Tool ### Operation 1. Select SCULPT mode on the menu select menu at the top right of Marvelous Designer. The Brush toolbar appears in the upper left corner of the SCULPT mode screen. 2. Select a Brush tool from Brush toolbar. When mouseover on 3D garment after selecting a brush tool, can check brush Size and Focal setting. 3. With a brush is selected, brush property will be displayed. Adjust Strenght, Size, Focal, Spacing Depth on Brush property. Also can change brush type and property setting on 3D window pop up menu (shortcut:B). 4. Click and drag on 3D garment to sculpt. Press the Shift key on the keyboard while using any type of Brush tool. 5. 3D garment will be displayed with gray in SCULPT mode. Adjust the color either material of 3D garment on Material Type on the property window. **Brush Types** Wrinkle | Left-click and drag to create wrinkles on the brush area. (ver. 10) ---|--- Release | Left-click + Shift and drag to release wrinkles on brush area. (ver. 10) Sculpt | Emboss mesh. With invert option activated, engraves mesh. Smooth | Makes the surface flat on average. (Shortcut: Shift) Grab | Moves vertexes to express pulled surface. Stamp | Use an image as a stamp. Pinch | Close the position of the vertexes, makes the surface sharper. **Brush Property** Depending on the type of brush, the properties you apply vary. Brush Property | Description | Brush Type ---|---|--- Wrinkle | Release | Sculpt | Smooth | Grab | Stamp | Pinch Simulation Preset | Simulation types that are applied when using Wrinkle and Release brush (ver. 10) | O | O | X | X | X | X | X Strength | Strength of brush. | X | X | O | O | O | O | O Size | Size of brush. | O | O | O | O | O | O | O Focal | Coverage of brush. (similar with Hardness) | O | O | O | O | O | O | O Spacing | Interval of brush. | X | X | O | X | X | X | X Depth | Depth of brush. | X | X | O | O | O | X | O Invert | Change the direction of a brush. (shortcut: Alt) | X | X | O | X | X | O | X Image | Using an image as brush. | X | X | O | X | O | O | X Realistic | Realistic (ver. 10) (Setting for Wrinkle, Release brush) | O | O | X | X | X | X | X Layer | Layer (ver. 10) (Setting for Wrinkle, Release brush) | O | O | X | X | X | X | X **Using an image as brush** 1. Click button next to Image. 2. Click an Image from default images. \- Focal setting is not available for image brush. 3. Click & Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. \- Click & Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. 4. To turn off an image, click button and select Off. \- Focal setting appears on brush property after turning off image. **Adding image** 1. Click + button next to image. 2. Select an image on the file browser. 3. Click & Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. \- Click & Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. 4. After adding image, can load the image by clicking button next to the image. **Creating image** Image file should be Black and white (mono-tone). White area emboss when using it as a brush. **Double Side Display** With Double Side option activated, can check both back and front side of mesh. **Show/Hide 3D Pattern (Shortcut Shift+Q)** 1. Show selected pattern only \- Select a pattern while input Shift+Q, other patterns will be hidden. 2. Reverse selected pattern/hidden pattern \- After operating no.1 above, click on the selected pattern while input Shift+Q to reverse hidden pattern/ selected pattern. 3. Adding hidden patterns \- To hide additional patterns, click on a pattern which you want to hide while input Shift+Q. 4. Show All 3D Patterns \- Click on the background while input Shift+Q to show all pattern. **3D Garment Rendering Style** You can set the following menus from the View Settings icon on the left of the 3D window. 1. Show Internal Lines 2. Monochrome Surface (Alt+3) / Wireframe on Surface (Alt+6)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to using the SCULPT mode brush tools in Marvelous Designer for creating and enhancing garment designs.

title: Free Sewing (2D)
content: ### Objective Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Free Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Free Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Free Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Free Sewing 2. Click, drag and click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. 3. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. → Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. 4. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. 5. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. ※ Note: * The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. * Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. * When establishing the second half of the seam, difference in the Sewing Line lengths appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. If the difference exceeds 1 inch, the difference appears in red to alert the user. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Free Sewing.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to freely establish Sewing Lines on pattern outlines and internal shapes, facilitating seamless design and precision in their sewing projects.

title: Apply Graphic Image
content: ### Objective Place graphic images on Patterns. Use this function to express Garment details such as placed prints, embroideries, or logos. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ Graphic (2D Pattern) / Graphic (3D Pattern) 3D or 2D Toolbar ▶ Graphic.png Graphic (2D Pattern) / Graphic (3D Pattern) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Graphic.png Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2. The file browser appears. → Select a graphic image file and load. 3. Click on a Pattern where the graphic image should be placed. → The Add Graphic window appears. 4. Enter the desired values for the graphic dimensions and position: Width | Set the width of the graphic image. ---|--- Height | Set the height of the graphic image. ![Captura de pantalla \(111\).png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438341118361) | Link or unlink the aspect ratio of the graphic image. Position | Outline | Set the distance from the left, right, top, or bottom of the graphic outline to the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (Ver. 2.5.0). Center | Set the distance from the center of the graphic to the left, right, top, or bottom of the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (Ver. 2.5.0). 5. Click OK to place the graphic image. ※ Note: * Add graphics directly by right-clicking on a thumbnail of an image file in the Library window, then select Add as Graphic from the pop-up menu (ver2.4.0). * When importing an AI file with multiple artboards as a graphic, the AI/PDF window appears where artboards can be reviewed and the desired artboard can be selected (Ver. 4.0.0). * PBR maps for Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, and Metalness channel can be automatically generated for the applied graphic image using PBR Map Generator (ver. 2024.1)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for placing graphic images on garment patterns to enhance design details through precise positioning and dimension settings.

title: Add Point to Intersection
content: Objective Add Segment Points to where segments intersect. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select the segment that is crossed. → The selected segment is highlighted in yellow. 3. Right click on the selected segment. → A pop-up menu appears. 4. Select the Add Point to Intersection option. → A Segment Point is added to where the segment intersects. ※Note: * The point is only added to the selected segment. * To add points to both intersecting segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select both segment before right-clicking and selecting Add Point to Intersection option.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding segment points at intersections in a 2D pattern editing tool.

title: MODULAR MODE: Create Custom Blocks
content: ### Objective Create a Block of a desired Garment and apply it to your design. ### Location Open Modular Template Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ▶ Modular Template Presets Load and Place Patterns Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor Sew Patterns to Block Boxes Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ### Operation Open Modular Template 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ▶ Modular Template Presets → Modular Template Presets window appears. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438578872601) ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438590200217) 2\. Select a desired Garment category and Modular Template type, click OK. → The selected Modular Template appears in the 2D window. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438579247385) Load and Place Patterns 1\. With a Modular Template opened, follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 2\. Add desired Garment files to place into the Block Boxes. 3\. From the added Garment files, click and drag the Patterns to the matching Block Boxes. → The Patterns are linked into the Block Boxes and Block Boxes turn into dark grey. 4\. Sew Patterns to Block Boxes, then Simulate. Sew Patterns to Block Boxes 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 2\. Click on Segment Sewing or Free Sewing tool. 3.Sew Patterns and Block Boxes. → Sewn parts of the Block Boxes turn into darker grey. ※ Note: * Block Boxes are sewn together by default. * Patterns that are sewn alone (i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. * Difference in length between the actual Patterns and the Block Boxes has no effect on the Simulation. * Rest of the principle is the same as the Simulation Mode. * To show Sewing Lines between Block Boxes and Patterns, activate the Show Modular Sewing/Show Pattern Sewing tool. This tool is activated by default in the Modular Mode. Click it again to either hide or show all Sewing Lines.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and applying a garment block to your design using the Modular Template in Modular Mode.

title: Guide for Installing Network Offline Version in the Same Network Environment
content: ### Guide for Installing Network Offline Version in the Same Network Environment ### Objective Install Network version in the same Network Environment when Server (PC connected to the red HASP Key) is unable to recognize Client (PC to run the software). ### 1.) Check-up on HASP Driver Installation on Server PC Operation 1\. Access to the Web Browser: [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) Check Sentinel HASP Driver is installed and operating on Server as shown in the image below. ![000.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438682562457) 2\. If the web page does not appear, reinstall Sentinel HASP Driver. [**HASP Driver Install Guide**](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585) ### ### 2.) Additional Set-up ACC Page on Client PC ### Operation 1\. Set up ACC page on PC you want to run the software. 2\. ACC Page : [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 3\. Click on Configuration (the red box in the image below). ![2323.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438693330457) 4\. Click Access to Remote License Managers. ![4545.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438682830361) 5\. Check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses' (image below) and type the Server PC IP in "Specify Search Parameters" then click Submit. ※ Note: How to check your IP: Windows Search ▶ Search 'Cmd.exe' ▶ Type 'ipconfig' [http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/](https://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/) ![4444.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438683135257) 6\. Wait for 10 seconds and its completed when HASP key page shows up (image below). If the page does not show up, the Server and Client may possibly be connected to different network environment. In that case, follow the link below, follow the guideline and try again. [Guideline for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358458287641) ![6666.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438683220121)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for installing the Network Offline Version of the software within the same network environment, ensuring proper recognition of the client PC by the server connected to the HASP key.

title: Elastic
content: ### Objective Insert elastic to the outer/internal lines of a Pattern to express shirring details. ### Location Pattern Property Editor ▶ Select a Line ▶ Elastic ### Operation 1. Select a outer or internal line with Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Pattern Property Editor ▶ Select a Line ▶ Elastic 3. Click the checkbox and set it On. 4. Adjust the intensity and ratio of the elastic. ※ Note: #### Elastic Properties Elastic | Decides whether to insert an elastic or not. Even though adjusting the value of intensity and ratio is not going to be applied, if this is not being checked. ---|--- Strength | Increase or decrease the elastic intensity value. Even if elastic that has the same ratio, may be affected differently depending on their intensity. Ratio | Shows the elastic ratio when the selected segment is set at 100%. Various garment can be expressed by adjusting the elastic ratio. The elastic ratio can be set up to 200% of the maximum segment. Length | Adjusts the elastic when the length value is entered. If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied to each segment. Entire Length | If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied as the total length of the combined segments.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for applying elastic to the lines of a pattern to enhance shirring details in garment design.

content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to displaying FBX imported cameras in the 3D window through the main menu.

title: Roll Up (ver. 12.2)
content: ## Feature Overview Makes it easier to fold the ends of garments, such as sleeve openings, pants openings, etc. ### Steps 1\. Select an outline of the 2D pattern with the Edit Pattern tool. \- Roll Up does not work on outlines contains a sewing relationship to another pattern. \- Roll Up might not work on some segment lines as this feature is optimized for sleeve openings and pants openings that creates a tube. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below. \- In 2D Window select a segment line, Right Mouse Button click ▶ Roll Up 3\. The Roll Up dialog box appears. Enter the desired input. Number of Roll Up | Set the number of Roll up to 3 times. ---|--- Distance | Enter a minimum of 10mm and a maximum of 200mm as the distance of each roll up Reset | While the dialog box is running, reset the applied Roll Up. Returning the garment to its original state. Apply | Apply Roll Up based on the input values entered. Close | Close the Roll Up dialog box. \- Once you enter the Number of Roll Up and Distance, a green circle will be displayed at the end position of the final garment in the 3D Window as a preview. \- Roll Up does not apply symmetrically or to instance modifications. ### End Result Select Close at the bottom of the dialog to exit Roll Up. \- If the Particle Distance of the pattern being rolled up is over 10mm, it will be automatically adjusted to 10 for stable simulation.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for using the Roll Up feature to easily fold garment openings in a 3D pattern design software.

title: Project with Meta Data (*.ZPrj)/ Garment with Meta Data (*.zpac)
content: ### Objective When saving Project files, an accompanying XML file with Garment, trim, and texture information will be provided. Turntable images will also be generated with the Project file (versions after 3.1.38) XML File Contents 1\. Product version 2\. Garment version 3\. Garment polygon, triangle, vertex count: this includes the pattern, trims, textures; all information related to the Garment. 3-1. Pattern polygon, triangle, vertex count 3-2. Trim Object polygon, triangle, vertex count: Trim are Object files imported via File » Import » Import as Trim. 3-3. Button polygon, triangle, and vertex count 3-4. Print Texture polygon, triangle, vertex count: Print Texture are textures imported as Graphic. 3-5. Texture Count: the number of textures applied to Fabric. 3-6. Material Count: the number of items used or applied to Fabric. 4\. Avatar total polygon, triangle, and vertex count 5\. Turntable image names --- ### Location Save as Project: Main Menu Save As Project with Metadata/ Garment with Meta Data ### Operation Save as Project 1. Navigate to the menu listed in Location. Save File window will appear. 2. Navigate to the desired file location. 3. Enter a file name in File Name, then click the Save button. 4. The Save Metadata dialogue will appear. File | Save Folder | Saves the Project file along with the metadata and turntable images within a folder. ---|---|--- Save .zip File | Saves the Project file along with the metadata and turntable images as a ZIP file. Image | Image Count | Select the number of images for the Turntable. *** Don't Show Again Check Box** Checking this box will hide the dialog, but will remember the last entered settings when saving the metadata. To view the dialog again, go to Main Menu » User Settings » Others » Metadata, then set the Don't Show Again Save Metadata option to Off.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on saving project files with associated XML metadata and turntable images, detailing the contents of the XML file and the steps to effectively save and manage garment-related data.

title: Move with Arrow Keys (3D)
content: ### Objective Select Patterns in the 3D window, then use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move them in specific increments. ### Location #### Move Patterns with Arrow Keys Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move #### Set Specific Movement Increment Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Arrow Key Movement Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Arrow Key Movement ### Operation #### Move Patterns with Arrow Keys 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move 2. Select Patterns or trims in the 3D window. → Selected Patterns or trims are highlighted in yellow. 3. Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the selected Pattern or trim. Arrow Keys | Description ---|--- ▲ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive y-axis. The Garment moves upwards. ▼ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative y-axis. The Garment moves downwards. ◀ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative x-axis. The Garment moves to the left. ▶ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive x-axis. The Garment moves to the right. ▲+ Ctrl | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative z-axis. The Garment moves away from you. ▼+ Ctrl | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive z-axis. The Garment moves towards you. #### Set Specific Movement Increment 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Arrow Key Movement Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Arrow Key Movement 2. Enter the desired distance moved with each arrow key input.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for selecting and moving patterns in a 3D environment using keyboard arrow keys, along with guidance on setting specific movement increments.

title: Create Buttonholes along Pattern Outline (Ver. 5.1)
content: ### Objective Create buttonholess along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole ### Operation **Create** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole 2. Right click on a Pattern Outline. → The Create Buttons/Buttonholes along Pattern Outline window appears. ※Note: To select multiple lines, press down the Shift key and click the lines to be selected. 3. Configure below options as needed: Start Position | Distance | Set the distance between the buttonholes and the selected line. ---|---|--- Interval | Set the distance between the buttonholes and the Pattern Outline. Reverse | The direction of which buttonholes are created is reversed to the Start Point. Replicate | Interval | Adjust the distance between the buttonholes. Number of Button/Buttonholes | Adjust the number of buttonholes to be created. 4. Click OK. → Buttonholes are created as a group. **Select** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Click on a buttonhole or a Pattern Outline where buttonholes are created. → All buttonholes in a group are selected. ※Note: Click again while the group of buttonholes are selected to select a single buttonhole. 3. Change selected buttonholes' properties or style or use right-click pop-up menu. → Any changes made are applied to all buttonholes in the same group. → Group information cannot be copied or duplicated. → A pop-up menu is available when right-clicking above the group line with the buttonhole tool. ※Note: Grouped buttonholes cannot be moved. **Unlink** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Right click on the buttonholes or the Pattern Outline and select Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes. → The link between the buttonholes are removed.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating, selecting, and unlinking buttonholes along a pattern outline using the Buttonhole 3D Toolbar.

title: Internal Ellipse
content: ### Objective Create internal ellipses or circles within Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Ellipse ### Operation #### Create Internal Ellipse 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Ellipse 2. Click and drag within a Pattern to freehand an ellipse. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a circle. 3. Release the mouse to complete the Internal Ellipse or the Internal Circle. ※ Note: While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a full circle by its center point (ver.5.1.0). #### Create Internal Ellipse with Entered Values 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Ellipse 2. Click once within a Pattern. → The Create Ellipse window appears. 3. Enter the desired values. Diameter | Set the diameter of the Internal Circle. ---|--- Radius | Set the radius of the Internal Circle (ver3.2.0). Link to maintain the width and height ratio. Circumference | Set the circumference of the Internal Circle (ver3.2.0). Position | To Outline | Set the position of the left, right, top, and bottom of the Internal Circles from the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). To Center | Set the position of the center of the Internal Circle from the left, right, top, and bottom of the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: Internal Shape Tool Group
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating internal ellipses or circles within patterns using the 2D Pattern creation tools.

title: Updating Network Software License
content: To update existing Software License Key due to renewing license or adding copies, please follow the instruction below. 1\. Generate C2V file with**the RUS executable file** , located at the bottom of this post, and submit your C2V file through [**this page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (Logging in with your Company ID is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com ![mceclip0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438742023449) 2\. The Marvelous Designer Team will send back a V2C file for your license update. 3\. Update the received V2C file by directing the RUS to the folder location of your V2C file at the bottom of the "Apply License File" tab and then clicking "Apply Update". ![2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438742207641) ### Double checking an updated License Key If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and access to [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 2\. Make sure all the information is in this part. 3\. Click Features once you see the key info. ![6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438742446745) 4\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed correctly. ![7.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438742615065)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for updating your Software License Key after renewing your license or adding copies, ensuring a smooth and efficient process.
